name: sh2-string-op-table
description: The shared catalog of string operations in the A1 param/runtime family (core request frontends-string-op-table-20260806): op -> A1 shape -> runtime behavior. Each frontend language has these natively (py .strip()/split(","), go strings.TrimSpace/Split, fish string trim/split, perl s/// + split, zsh ${(s:,:)}); the shared shape exists ONCE here so a language op maps to one testable A1 shape instead of a per-frontend invention. The authoritative implementation is `sh2.param` (harness/sh2-namespace.mjs, ~line 2777) and the split/join helpers; whitelisted helper names are in src/shir_json.rs (purity table).

param_call_shape.note: the value is read from the store (`getVar(name)`) at runtime; the emitter may inline lifted bindings as a trailing `value` argument

slice.runtime: offset/len may be arithmetic strings; array names slice the array (`${#arr[@]}` length and `${!map[@]}` keys ride this op)

assign_default.runtime: if empty: setVar(name, default) and return it

split.runtime: default (unset or whitespace-only IFS): whitespace collapse (split(/\s+/) + drop empties); custom IFS (frontends-ifs 20260806): split on the IFS chars, KEEPING empty fields between adjacent separators; empty IFS: NO splitting
split.explicit_separator: zsh flag form: param("", name, flags, sep) with s/j flags (${(s:,:)x}); a frontend needing split(sep) without zsh may emit split() and set IFS, or use the flag form
split.field_split_marker: the A1 `split` marker on UNQUOTED expansions (for-iters `for w in $y`, exec args `set -- $y`, array-literal elements `arr=($y)`)

join.a1: array joins: `$x[*]` joins with IFS[0] (quoted `${x[*]}` too); `$x[@]` joins with a space; positional `$*` joins with IFS[0]
join.explicit_separator: zsh flag form: param("", name, flags, sep) with the j flag (${(j:,:)x})

gate: cargo test --lib stays green; two frontends lowering the same language op to the SAME A1 shape (from this table) is the acceptance signal
